newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says attack on peso to be short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Manila says attack on peso to be short-lived.

text.p: The speculative attack on the Philippine peso is likely to be short-lived, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday.
"We are entering a period where there is a strong speculative attack on the peso which in our opinion is not exactly in keeping with normal market forces," he said.
"This is a speculative attack which has to be put in its place over the short span of time that I think it will be taking place."
"I think it is incumbent upon us to stem the tide so the peso does not depreciate simply because of the machinations of some who are trying to put pressure on it," de Ocampo said.

The peso came under fresh attack on Wednesday following a Singapore newspaper report quoting a government minister -- who later said his remarks had been "twisted" -- that the government was considering a devaluation.
De Ocampo reiterated that the government would continue its policy of allowing the rate to be determined by market forces, as long as the movement was not due to speculators.

The speculation against the peso has also followed the financial crisis in Thailand, but de Ocampo said too much attention was paid to the similarities and not the differences between the two economies.
He felt the market had so far reacted positively to the Central Bank's actions to defend the currency.
"As of now we think it is adequately defended and of course we are looking at the situation day to day," he said, when asked if the government planned to take interest rates higher.
On Monday, the Central Bank pushed overnight interest rates to their highest in 2-1/2 years at 30 percent.
